answer: Agents can require reputation to come from signed attestations by distinct peers who each lock stake, while capping each peer’s influence. New identities must build trust through useful work; they cannot instantly copy a credible history. If collusion is detected, the system slashes the backing stake, sending a ripple through the attacker’s network. The attacker pays in locked capital, time, and risk—not just account creation. This ridge of checks raises the cost of flooding an ocean of identities.
